03 · Solution summary

Ask one question.
Mobilise the right expertise.

GxP Sentinel is a local multi-agent assurance workspace. It routes a bounded question to specialist agents, verifies every finding against evidence, and gates consequential actions through a human decision.

1 · User intentQuestion, selected system, role and scope.

A1 · Specialist

System Knowledge Agent

Answers system-specific questions using approved documents, system records, incident history, access reviews and supplier evidence.

  • Retrieves only relevant, authorised evidence.
  • Links answers to source IDs and metadata.
  • Escalates when evidence is missing or contradictory.
Boundary: Explains evidence; never invents a missing record.
04 · Technical implementation

A multi-agent system.
Inside a control plane.

One local model supports seven logical agents, while deterministic services own measurable findings, confidence, permissions, approvals and audit integrity.

Drag to pan · wheel to zoom
Zoom 100%
01

Local agent runtime

Seven role-specific agents share one local instruction model, separate prompts, tools, schemas and boundaries.

02

Deterministic control engine

Dates, approvals, traceability gaps, privileges, confidence and action policy are calculated in code.

03

Local retrieval & data

SQLite search, metadata filters and local file ingestion support MD, TXT, CSV, JSON, PDF, DOCX and XLSX.

04

Evidence graph

Requirements connect to risk, design, test, executed evidence and change history.

05

Policy + action gateway

Least privilege, server-trusted payloads and human approval prevent unbounded autonomy.

06

Traceable assurance

Prompt-injection scanning, bounded budgets, audit events and a SHA-256 hash chain make control operation visible.

Models / algorithms

One local instruction model for intent and narrative; deterministic rule services for findings, scoring, confidence and approvals.

Data sources

Synthetic controlled documents, requirements/tests, incidents, access records, risk, changes, suppliers and backup evidence.

Evaluation

Seven reversible Assurance Lab scenarios, evidence-grounding checks, permission checks and 9/9 visible local safety controls.

Limitations discovered

Local model latency varies by hardware; image-only PDFs require OCR outside this prototype; enterprise identity, scale, connector performance and production validation are not yet demonstrated. The readiness indicator is not a compliance certification.

Robustness · What happens when AI goes wrong?

Break the demo.
Watch it fail safely.

Seven reversible synthetic scenarios make modern agentic risks visible to judges — and show the exact control that contains each failure.

S1

Indirect prompt injection

Malicious instruction embedded in evidence.

S2

Stale SOP

Expired source tries to support a current conclusion.

S3

Conflicting evidence

Two sources disagree on approval status.

S4

Privileged orphan

A former-vendor account retains elevated access.

S5

Write without approval

A GxP-relevant operation attempts execution.

S6

Runaway task

An agent exceeds its bounded runtime budget.

S7

Memory poisoning

Untrusted content attempts to become persistent memory.

Ready. Select a scenario to test the control plane.
06 · Feasibility & roadmap

Prototype proven.
Scale with control.

The safest next move is a staged adoption path: prove value with read-only evidence, qualify controls and data, then introduce limited enterprise actions behind existing approvals.

M1 · 0–8 weeks

Controlled pilot

Use synthetic or sanitised evidence with System Managers and QA. Baseline time, quality and user trust.

M2 · 2–4 months

Read-only connectors

Integrate permission-bound views of Service Management, document, validation and access sources.

M3 · 4–8 months

Assurance & governance

Complete intended-use, risk, cybersecurity, validation/CSA, SOP, monitoring and performance evidence.

M4 · 8–12 months

Controlled scale

Expand to selected systems and enable allowlisted workflow actions with human approval and rollback.

D
Data availability & quality

Source metadata, approvals and links may be incomplete or inconsistent.

Mitigation: data contracts, trust states, reconciliation and explicit abstention.

I
Integration effort

Enterprise APIs, permissions and source semantics differ by platform.

Mitigation: typed read-only adapters, least privilege and phased source onboarding.

G
GxP / regulatory assurance

Production use requires intended-use, risk-based validation and controlled lifecycle evidence.

Mitigation: keep AI advisory, rules deterministic, decisions human and traceability complete.

A
Adoption & over-reliance

Users may over-trust concise AI narratives or resist a new workflow.

Mitigation: evidence-first UX, role training, calibrated confidence and visible limitations.

Evidence & assumptions

Demonstrated in the local prototype: a 10-minute review sequence, seven agents, five example gaps, local/offline operation, 9/9 visible safety controls, evidence graph, human approval and evidence-pack export. Financial benefit, enterprise latency, scale and production-quality outcomes require pilot measurement.

The three things to remember

Audit-ready is not a moment.
It is a continuously visible state.

01

Evidence, not eloquence.

Every material conclusion carries source IDs, freshness, confidence, uncertainty and a retained trace.

02

Multi-agent, not uncontrolled autonomy.

Specialists collaborate inside deterministic policy, bounded budgets and human approval.

03

Local-first. Enterprise-ready.

The working prototype proves the journey now and provides a controlled path to read-only integration and scaled assurance.
